messages:
alerts-bot: SLO ALERT - hosted-infer.usw2.gateway p99(5xx+timeouts) = 0.87 > 0.5 (3m)
Alex (SRE): seeing it, digging in.
Priya (SRE): i'm pulling traces + logs now. any customer hits?
Jorge (Support): customer C-5921 reported repeated 502 + timeouts starting ~11:40 PDT, says it affects a handful of users. forwarded sample request.
Marina (DevEx): flagged on Slack thread with account team. asking if this looks auth/billing related.
Priya (SRE): running quick logs query:
```
index=prod_logs service=gateway status>=500 | span_id!=null | count by upstream_cluster, host | sort -count
```
Priya (SRE): results: spike from upstream cluster infer-backend-eu with host=proxy-12, proxy-13, p50 backend latency went from ~30ms to 800ms in that window. also a large fraction of traces have missing spans (sampling/gap).
Alex (SRE): interesting — backend latency + trace gaps -> either a slow upstream or intermittent handshake failure. can someone check edge TLS handshakes / keepalive?
sre-oncall: running tcpdump on proxy-12 now.
Jorge (Support): customer says they rotated billing tokens at 11:38. we see a few 401s earlier in request logs, but now mostly 502/504.
Alex (SRE): post the sample request headers here (sanitize token) — looking for mismatch in X-Customer-Billing / Authorization order.
Jorge (Support): sample sanitized: 
```
POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
X-Customer-Billing-Token: <rotated-redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
```
Priya (SRE): quick trace check: for a subset of requests, gateway forwarded to infer-backend-eu but backend returned 502 and closed stream; traces end at gateway with no upstream span -> trace gap.
Priya (SRE): hypothesis: upstream pool overloaded after token rotation (new tokens caused authz check miss -> backend spun up auth retries and overwhelmed connection pool) or intermittent auth-control plane failure.
Alex (SRE): can we repro locally against that upstream? try hitting a proxy instance with the rotated token and low QPS to see handshake/retry behaviour.
Marina (DevEx): I created a temporary dashboard and pinned the following panels: p99 latency (gateway), 5xx fraction by upstream, auth 401s by token hash. https://grafana.internal/d/abc/hosted-infer-slo
Priya (SRE): repro steps i used:
1) export REDWOOD_TOKEN=<rotated>
2) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" -H "X-Customer-Billing-Token: $BILL_TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
Observed: 1/5 requests return 502 with connection reset, 4/5 succeed.
Priya (SRE): curl verbose shows `upstream prematurely closed connection` and gateway logs show `upstream response: code=502 proto_err` for same request ids.
Alex (SRE): low repro rate but consistent pattern -> likely transient upstream stateful resource (connection pool / kv cache). can we correlate with prefetch/batcher logs?
Priya (SRE): checked batcher: around 11:39 we see a restart in kv-cache consumer on infer-backend-eu-2 (OOM/restart) which led to backlog. that matches timeline.
Alex (SRE): OOM + restart would cause some in-flight requests to hit 502 and trace gaps. also explains p99 spike.
Jorge (Support): customer impacted by a handful of failed calls; billing team worried about token rotation causing break. they want mitigation ASAP.
Marina (DevEx): temporary mitigation options: 1) expand upstream connection pool; 2) increase prefetch timeouts; 3) disable aggressive retry/fanout for affected route; 4) fallback routing to dedicated variant for that customer.
Alex (SRE): immediate action: flip routing policy to failover to infer-backend-usw variant for customer "acct-913". Priya, can you push canary?
Priya (SRE): will push canary + increase upstream pool by 20% on proxy-12/13. deploying now.
sre-oncall: applying config patch: `route.acct-913.priority=[usw, eu]` and `upstream.pool.size+=20%` to proxy-12/13.
Priya (SRE): canary up, traffic for acct-913 routed to usw variant for 2% of requests, latency p99 trending down for that cohort.
Alex (SRE): also setting a temporary gate: reduce gateway concurrency for that route to avoid creating new in-flight requests while backend recovering.
Jorge (Support): told customer we routed around the hotspot and reduced error rate; collecting logs for their postmortem. they asked for ETA on full fix.
Priya (SRE): full fix: replace failing backend node, bump memory limit to avoid OOM, add defensive retry/backoff in auth control plane. Ops ticket created: IS-1746.
Marina (DevEx): filing follow-up runbook item: when p99(5xx+timeouts) triggers and traces show >20% missing upstream spans -> check for backend restarts (k8s events), kv-cache consumer restarts, and token rotation correlation. link runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/infer-gateway-5xx
Alex (SRE): assign postmortem to Priya and Alex. Priya please include timeline, root cause (OOM->trace gap->5xx spike), mitigation steps, and customer comms.
Priya (SRE): will draft PM and runbook update.
alerts-bot: SLO ALERT RESOLVED - p99 back to 0.32.
Jorge (Support): customer confirmed reduced errors, will follow up if anything else.
Alex (SRE): closing thread, will link PM when ready. :thumbsup:
